Visual design review · 23 November 2026

The engine is ahead of the looks

Radiant can hold a 5,000-node map in a single branch draw call, and it already has themes, tapered branches, AI pictures and a presentation view. The canvas still reads as a correct diagram, not something you would want to show someone. The gap is craft in a few specific places, and most of it sits in four files.

Both panels are SVG illustrations generated for this report. Real app screenshots are in How it looks today.

564commits, 17–18 Nov 2026
267 / 341requirements with direct acceptance evidence
7built-in themes, 5 branch styles
8visual findings, 18 recommendations

The five moves that matter most

  1. Fix four geometry flaws that show in every screenshot. Faceted curves, branches piling onto one point at the root, square line ends and a root that looks like a disabled button.
  2. Give the type a voice. Every theme uses the system font. macOS ships rounded, serif and handwriting faces that cost nothing to offer.
  3. Add depth and colour movement. Soft shadows, tips that lighten, and a canvas with some surface to it.
  4. Ship showpiece themes. Six concepts are drawn below. The first choice a user makes should be between looks, not settings.
  5. Make maps memorable and shareable. A tintable illustration library, branches that grow in as the AI writes, and an export that frames the map like a poster.

01 · InventoryWhat has been built

Radiant is a local-first macOS mind-map editor: Svelte and TypeScript on a custom WebGL2 renderer, a Rust/Tauri host and single-file SQLite documents. This is what exists today that affects how a map looks.

AreaWhat existsWhere
RendererWebGL2 with multisampling, instanced rounded rectangles drawn as distance fields, a label atlas, and all branches in one mesh. A 5,000-node map with 300 pictures uses one branch draw call.src/lib/render/
ThemesClean, Buzan strict, Buzan relaxed, Hand-drawn, Plain outline, Midnight, Ink. Each has a dark variant. A theme editor covers colours, fonts, shapes, gaps and widths, and personal themes can be saved.core/model/themes.ts
BranchesRounded, angular, tapered, organic and line. Width decays by 0.58 per level: 14 → 8.12 → 4.71 → 2.73 units.core/geometry/
Node shapesBox, rectangle, circle, square, underline, none.core/model/theme-settings.ts
LayoutsBalanced, right, left, down, up, radial, compact, outline, timeline, columns, grid and popcorn, plus seeded organic variation.core/layout/
LabelsCurved labels for Latin, Greek and Cyrillic, uppercase main branches, keyword labels, numbered markers and emoji stickers.render/text.ts
ArtworkAI pictures per node with a style reference, AI-drawn SVG subtrees, a central image, on-device cutouts and pen sketches.core/art/, core/ai/
MotionFold and unfold over 220 ms, camera moves over 350 ms with a cubic ease, streamed nodes animate in, and Reduce Motion is honoured.ui/layout-animation.ts:4, render/camera.ts:7
ViewsFocus on a branch, a filter that dims the rest to 22%, a full-screen presentation that steps through branches, and a minimap.ui/controller.svelte.ts
ExportPNG with scale and transparency, SVG, PDF and print, plus Markdown, OPML, FreeMind and JSON Canvas.ui/ExportPanel.svelte
Quality gatesFive pixel-compared reference images, and a contrast check across 308 colour pairs with a 4.69:1 minimum.requirements/

02 · EvidenceHow it looks today

These are real captures from the current code, taken on 23 November 2026 with the development server in Chrome at 2× pixel density, using the same 31-node map in four themes.

03 · DiagnosisEight findings

Each finding is something visible in the captures above, traced to the code that causes it.

1

Curves are drawn as short straight segments

Bends show corners, most clearly where a thick branch turns into a label underline. The segment count depends only on branch length and never rises when you zoom in, so the corners grow with zoom.

core/geometry/tessellate.ts:86 — n = round((4 + chord × 0.045) × lod), clamped to 3–32, and lod never exceeds 1.

2

Main branches pile onto one point at the root

Every main branch on a side starts at the centre of the root's edge. They overlap into a blob, and whichever is drawn last covers the others. Here yellow hides orange, and purple hides pink.

core/geometry/branches.ts:105 — the start point uses only the side, not the child's position.

3

The root looks like a disabled button

The centre of the map is the least designed thing on it: a grey pill with a dark outline and no elevation. The fill is the root colour mixed at 18% over the background, which always lands on grey.

core/geometry/style.ts:183 — fill strength 0.18 for the root, 0.12 for other boxes.

4

Lines end square

Underlines stop with a flat cut, and thin leaf branches end abruptly. A round cap is built only at the start of each branch.

core/geometry/tessellate.ts:296 — start cap only. The underline quad has no end cap.

5

Buzan strict has no centre

The preset removes the root shape because it expects a central image. Until one is added, six heavy branches run into bare text and overlap its first and last letters.

core/model/themes.ts — rootShape: 'none' with a 22-unit root branch width.

6

Hand-drawn is half committed

Box outlines wobble and branches wave, which is a good start. The type is still the system sans, the strokes have clean vector edges, and the paper is a flat colour, so it reads as a tidy diagram on beige.

core/geometry/hand-drawn.ts:8 wobbles rectangles only.

7

There is one typeface

Every built-in theme uses the system font. The theme editor offers four more: Arial, Georgia, Trebuchet MS and Courier New. None of them gives a theme a character of its own.

core/model/themes.ts:4 and core/model/theme-settings.ts:5.

8

Nothing has depth or colour movement

Boxes are a flat fill and a stroke. Branches are one flat colour from trunk to tip, although the mesh already stores a colour per vertex. The canvas is a flat colour or a dot grid. Six of the seven dark variants share one palette, so they look alike. Selection is a generic blue ring.

render/shaders.ts:65 (rectangle shader), core/model/themes.ts:110 (dark variants).

04 · ResearchWhat other products do

I searched for how other mind-map and canvas tools make their maps attractive and memorable. Most of what follows comes from the vendors' own pages and release notes, so read the feature claims as theirs. I did not use the products.

MindNode

Mac · closest peer
  • 260+ hand-crafted stickers with adjustable colours
  • Hierarchical themes that style each level separately
  • Themes that follow light and dark mode (2025.4)
  • Focus Mode dims everything but one branch (2025.2)
  • Tapered branches, radial layout and new node shapes arrived in 2026.4

For Radiant: You already have tapering and radial. The gap is the sticker library and how finished each theme feels.

Xmind

Cross-platform
  • One click switches a map to a hand-drawn look
  • Nine rainbow schemes for coloured branches, and colour themes of six colours each
  • Up to 31 topic shapes
  • Nearly 500 stickers and illustrations
  • Pitch Mode turns a map into slides with generated transitions
  • Map Shot exports an image with frame, shadow and watermark options

For Radiant: Palettes as a separate choice from structure, and an export built for sharing, are the two ideas most worth taking.

Ayoa

Buzan lineage
  • Organic style modelled on the hand-drawn mind map
  • Curved branches you bend by dragging control points
  • Thickness that tapers from a heavy trunk to fine tips
  • Images attached to branches, with image search built in

For Radiant: Its whole identity is the organic branch. Radiant's organic style has the geometry and needs the finish.

MindMeister

Web
  • 2017 themes made topic bubbles bigger and rounder and added ten fonts
  • Reviewers single out its clean interface and automatic alignment
  • One-click presentation from the editor

For Radiant: Round, friendly shapes and a wider choice of type are a cheap route to an approachable look.

SimpleMind

Cross-platform
  • Over 15 style sheets, each switchable to dark
  • Styling by level or by branch
  • Borders drawn around a branch or a group

For Radiant: Group borders are a visual device Radiant does not have yet.

Whimsical

Web · speed
  • Automatic formatting with a curated palette
  • Keyboard-first: Tab for a child, Enter for a sibling
  • Praised for connectors that stay attached as things move

For Radiant: A small, opinionated palette beats a colour picker for most people.

Miro

Whiteboard · cautionary
  • A long-running community request is titled "More visually appealing Mind maps" and calls them "very bland"
  • It asks for thicker branches, a more colourful centre and images on nodes
  • Users also object to angular connectors as the default

For Radiant: Users notice, and ask for, exactly the things this report recommends.

tldraw · Excalidraw

Hand-drawn canvases
  • tldraw seeds its imperfections with each shape's ID so they never jitter
  • It draws each stroke twice with different offsets for texture
  • Corners are softened with curves
  • Writers on Excalidraw say the rough style signals a working draft

For Radiant: Radiant already seeds per node. Two-pass strokes are the missing step for a convincing hand-drawn look.

Kinopio · Milanote

Spatial canvases
  • Kinopio keeps almost no toolbar so the content carries the personality
  • One comparison says Milanote boards look better for client-facing work

For Radiant: Presentation quality is a reason people choose a tool, separate from features.

06 · ProposalRecommendations

Eighteen changes in five tracks. Size is relative effort (S, M, L). Impact is my judgement of how much each changes a first impression.

Track A · Fix the craft

Small geometry changes that lift every theme at once. Do these first.

Curves

Root junction

Terminals and tint

Selection

A1

Smooth the curves

Choose the segment count from curvature and zoom so the polyline stays within a quarter of a pixel of the curve. Rebuild at a few zoom steps. The app already has a per-branch mesh cache, so only changed branches are rebuilt.

Fan the root joins

Spread main-branch start points along the root's edge in child order and let each leave in its own direction. Radial layouts already clip to the box outline, so the same routine can serve horizontal layouts.

Track B · A signature look

Type, depth and colour. These give each theme a character.

B1

Offer real typefaces

Add macOS faces to the font list: the rounded and serif system faces, Avenir Next, Noteworthy, Marker Felt and Chalkboard. They cost nothing to ship. Bundle two or three open-licence fonts later so exports look the same on other machines.

Seen in
MindMeister added ten fonts with its themes; MindNode downloads missing fonts
Where
theme-settings.ts:5
Size SImpact ●●●
B2

Soft shadows

The rectangle shader already computes a distance to the box edge. Widening that falloff gives a blurred shadow in the same draw call. Use it under the root, boxes and pictures.

Seen in
Xmind Map Shot shadows
Where
shaders.ts:65
Size MImpact ●●○
B3

Tint branches toward the tips

The branch mesh stores a colour for every vertex and currently writes the same one each time. Blend toward a lighter tint with depth, or toward a neighbouring hue in dark themes.

Offer eight to ten curated palettes as a choice separate from the theme. Run each through the existing contrast and colour-vision checks. Give each dark variant its own palette.

Track D · Motion and focus

The renderer draws only when something changes, so motion should be tied to an event and then stop.

D1

Grow branches in

When a node is created or streamed, extend its branch along the curve from the parent, then fade in the label. Streamed nodes already animate after layout, so this changes what the animation draws.

Seen in
Xmind Pitch Mode transitions
Where
ui/layout-animation.ts
Size MImpact ●●●
D2

Spring the layout moves

Fold, unfold and tidy use a fixed 220 ms ease. A lightly damped spring feels more physical and still settles quickly. Keep the Reduce Motion path as it is.

Seen in
General canvas-app practice; not from a specific source
Where
layout-animation.ts:4, camera.ts:7
Size SImpact ●○○
D3

Trace a branch on hover

Reuse the filter's dimming to fade everything except the hovered node's path to the root and its subtree.

Seen in
MindNode Focus Mode and tag highlight
Where
ui/canvas-filter.ts:10
Size SImpact ●●○
D4

Give the presentation a reveal

The presentation view already steps the camera through branches. Have each step grow its branch in and dim the ones not yet shown.

Xmind Pitch Mode; MindMeister presentation

Pictures and colour are what Buzan-style maps are built on, and what Miro users ask for by name.

Share card

An export preset that puts the map on a backdrop with padding, rounded corners, a shadow and a title line, sized for a slide or a post. Today's export gives a bare PNG, SVG or PDF with an optional transparent background.

07 · SequenceOrder of work

Each phase is useful on its own. Sizes are relative; I have not estimated days.

1 · Craft

A1–A5. Smooth curves, fanned joins, round ends, a designed root, coloured selection. Every existing theme improves.

5 × S
2 · Type and colour

B1, B3, B4. Typefaces, tip tinting and the palette library. No new rendering passes.

2 × S, 1 × M
3 · Depth and surface

B2, B5, B6. Shadows, canvas surfaces and the second hand-drawn pass. These need matching vector output in SVG and PDF export.

3 × M
4 · Themes

C1, C2. Assemble the presets from phases 1–3 and add the thumbnail picker.

2 × M
5 · Motion and sharing

D1–D4, E2, E3. Grow-in, springs, hover trace, presentation reveal, share card, group borders.

2 × S, 4 × M
6 · Illustrations

E1. The largest item, and mostly a content job: sourcing or drawing the set and tagging it.

1 × L

Constraints to design within

Frame budgetThe targets are an 8.3 ms frame and at most 4 ms of script while panning 5,000 nodes, with one branch draw call. Smoother curves mean more triangles, so measure A1 on the 5,000-node fixture.
Draw only on changeThe renderer makes zero draw calls when idle. That rules out ambient animation such as drifting backgrounds or pulsing glows.
Export must match the canvasSVG and PDF export are compared against the canvas. Gradients and shadows have vector equivalents. Grain does not, and I have not checked whether the PDF path supports SVG filters.
Contrast and colour visionLabels are held to 4.5:1 and themes are checked under three colour-vision simulations. New palettes and tints go through the same checks.
Picking follows geometryClicks are tested against the real branch outline. Fanned joins and end caps change that outline, so hit-testing changes with them.
Reference imagesFive tracked captures will fail on purpose after phase 1. Re-record them with tools/check-visuals.py --record and review the diffs.
Decoration can cost attentionThe project's own evidence review has a section headed "Decoration, emotion and load". I did not re-read it for this report. Keep effects per theme and keep the plain themes.
Shared contractscore/types.ts is marked coordinator-owned in ARCHITECTURE.md. New theme fields go through it.

08 · NotesMethod and sources

Project review. I read the commit history, README, ARCHITECTURE, both handoffs, the three requirement audits and the theme, style, geometry, shader and renderer source. Counts of commits and requirements come from git and the 18 November handoff.

Screenshots. Captured from the development server with the browser host in Chrome at 1440 × 900 and 2× density, using a 31-node map loaded through the app's own debug hook. I did not run the packaged macOS build.

Mockups. Every panel marked Today or Proposed, and every theme concept, is an SVG drawn for this report. The Today panels use the app's segment formula and attachment rule so the flaws are reproduced, not exaggerated. Nothing in the app was changed.

Competitor research. Web searches on 23 November 2026. Most sources are vendor pages, release notes and community forums. I did not install or use the products, and the size and impact ratings are my own judgement.
